ev.q: Among women aged 30–64 years, the unadjusted drug overdose death rate increased 260%
Crude rates are reported as deaths per 100,000 population.
The average age at death from overall drug overdoses among women aged 30–64 years increased by 2.8 years
from 6.7 deaths per 100,000 population (4,314 total drug overdose deaths) in 1999 to 24.3 (18,110) in 2017
The crude rate for deaths involving prescription opioids increased from 1999 to 2017 for every age group
Mortality data for U.S. residents were obtained from the 1999–2017 National Vital Statistics System
From 1999 to 2017, the crude rate of drug overdose deaths among women aged 30–64 years in the United States increased by 260%.

methods_quotes.q: was used to test the significance of overdose trends from 1999 to 2017
Annual percentage change estimates that were statistically significant (p<0.05) are presented
Percent change was calculated on unrounded rates.
Crude rates are reported as deaths per 100,000 population.
Age distribution changes in drug-specific overdose deaths were calculated by 5-year age groupings
Rates in 1999 for certain age groups are not displayed because counts were <20 deaths.
